t: A Gaelic kingdom straddling the North Channel, with lands in County Antrim and in Argyll, ruled from the rock fortress of Dunadd.
Columba’s monastery on Iona, founded under its kings in 563, carried Christianity and learning to the Picts and Northumbria.
Weakened by defeats and Pictish attack, it merged with Pictland in the ninth century, and its Gaelic speech became Scotland’s.
dyk: The summit of Dunadd bears a carved human footprint, a rock basin and a boar, which are thought to have been used in the inauguration of kings.
ev: Columba founds the monastery of Iona
Áedán mac Gabráin becomes king, ordained by Columba according to Adomnán
Æthelfrith of Northumbria defeats Áedán at the Battle of Degsastan
Domnall Brecc is defeated at the Battle of Mag Rath in Ireland
Óengus son of Fergus, king of the Picts, captures Dunadd
Viking raids on the Hebrides and Iona begin
Cináed mac Ailpín becomes king of the Picts
